A docking center is configured to facilitate communication between a dockee and a peripheral device connected to the docking center. In this role, the docking center manages connectivity and assists in coordinating communication so that the dockee can access or interact with the peripheral device.

Initially, the docking center operates as the group owner of a first group. While acting in this capacity, the docking center transmits information to the dockee that enables the dockee to establish a direct connection with the peripheral device. This information may include connection parameters, identification information, capability information, or other data needed by the dockee to set up the direct communication link.

The docking center may also receive, from the dockee, an assist request for establishing the direct connection with the peripheral device. In response to the assist request, the docking center determines whether the requested assistance can be provided and transmits a response indicating whether the assist request is accepted. If accepted, the docking center may assist in the setup of the direct connection according to the transmitted connection information.

In addition, the docking center may receive a release request related to the dockee and the peripheral device. Upon receiving the release request, the docking center releases its connections with both the dockee and the peripheral device. The docking center also terminates its control of the peripheral device, thereby allowing the dockee and the peripheral device to communicate directly without continued control by the docking center, or otherwise ending the docking center’s involvement in that peripheral connection.

The docking center may further receive a request to join a second group. In response, the docking center joins the second group as a client, while the dockee operates as the group owner of the second group. After joining the second group, the docking center continues to operate simultaneously as the group owner of the first group and as a client of the second group. In this dual role, the docking center maintains its group-owner functions for the first group while participating as a client in the second group managed by the dockee.

A docking center may assist communication between a dockee, such as a mobile computing device, and a peripheral device that is connected to or otherwise associated with the docking center. The docking center can maintain information about the peripheral device and about the communication environment in which the dockee, the docking center, and the peripheral operate. When the dockee seeks to communicate directly with the peripheral device, the docking center may provide the dockee with direct-connection information, such as addressing data, device identifiers, service identifiers, security parameters, channel information, pairing information, or other data needed to establish a direct communication link with the peripheral device.

In addition to providing such information, the docking center may participate in the setup procedure for the new connection. For example, the docking center may authenticate the dockee, authorize access to the peripheral device, exchange configuration data, negotiate capabilities, or relay setup messages between the dockee and the peripheral device. If the peripheral device is already linked to the docking center or to another group managed by the docking center, the docking center may release, suspend, or modify the existing link so that the peripheral device can be made available for direct access by the dockee. This release may be performed in an orderly manner so that ongoing sessions are terminated properly, resources are freed, and the peripheral device is prepared to accept a new controlling connection.

The docking center may also coordinate changes in group membership. Initially, the docking center may act as the owner or controller of an original communication group that includes the peripheral device. The dockee may be a member of that original group or may communicate with the docking center through a separate connection. When direct access to the peripheral is to be established, the docking center may help form a new communication group in which the dockee becomes the owner or controller. The peripheral device may then join the new group, allowing the dockee to communicate with and control the peripheral directly.

During this process, the docking center may continue to serve as the owner of the original group while also becoming a client or member of the new group created under the control of the dockee. In this dual role, the docking center can maintain management of its existing network or docking environment while still participating in, monitoring, or supporting the newly formed group. This arrangement allows the docking center to coordinate handoff of control without losing connectivity or management capability.

As a result, the dockee is able to obtain direct access to the peripheral device without requiring the docking center to remain in the data path for all subsequent communications. The peripheral can be controlled more efficiently by the dockee, while the docking center continues to provide support functions such as discovery, authorization, configuration, group coordination, and fallback management. This approach enables flexible use of connected peripherals, efficient transition of ownership or control, and smooth handoff between docking-center-managed communication and dockee-managed direct communication.

**Disclosed**

The word **“disclosed”** refers to something that has been revealed, made known, or shared openly. It is often used in legal, business, financial, and personal contexts when information that was previously private, confidential, or unknown becomes available to others.

In business, companies may be required to disclose important information to investors, customers, or government authorities. For example, a company might disclose its financial results, risks, partnerships, or conflicts of interest. This helps create transparency and allows people to make informed decisions.

In legal situations, disclosed information can include documents, evidence, agreements, or statements that must be shared between parties. Proper disclosure is important because it supports fairness and accountability.

The term can also apply to everyday life. A person may disclose personal information, such as their health condition, background, or feelings, when they choose to share it with someone else. In these cases, disclosure often requires trust and respect for privacy.

Overall, **disclosed** means that information has been openly revealed. Whether in law, business, or personal communication, disclosure plays an important role in honesty, transparency, and responsible decision-making.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent abstract for a docking center that assists direct communication between a dockee and a peripheral device using group owner/client roles.
counterfactuals.output: A docking center is provided for facilitating direct communication between a dockee device and a peripheral device. The docking center establishes a wireless communication group and assigns group owner and client roles to enable peer-to-peer connectivity. In one implementation, the docking center operates as a group owner to discover, authenticate, and associate the dockee and the peripheral device, and thereafter assists establishment of a direct communication link between the dockee and the peripheral device. The docking center may exchange connection parameters, security credentials, service information, and role assignment data with the dockee and the peripheral device, and may coordinate a transition in which one of the dockee or the peripheral device assumes a group owner role while the other operates as a client. After the direct link is established, data associated with the peripheral device is communicated directly with the dockee, reducing latency, bandwidth use, and processing load at the docking center while maintaining docking-session control.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a formal patent summary for a method performed by a docking center to facilitate communication between a dockee and a peripheral device, including transmitting connection information, handling assist/release/joining requests, and operating simultaneously as group owner and client.
counterfactuals.output:
A method performed by a docking center is provided for facilitating communication between a dockee and a peripheral device. The method includes establishing or maintaining a wireless communication environment in which the docking center is communicatively associated with the dockee and the peripheral device, and transmitting, to the dockee, connection information usable by the dockee to establish communication with the peripheral device. The connection information may include identification information, addressing information, authentication information, service information, or group-related information associated with the peripheral device or a wireless group in which the peripheral device participates.

The method further includes receiving, from the dockee, an assist request requesting assistance in connecting to or communicating with the peripheral device. In response to the assist request, the docking center may provide the dockee with connection parameters, perform discovery or negotiation procedures, relay control information, or otherwise facilitate establishment of a communication path between the dockee and the peripheral device. The method may also include receiving a release request from the dockee or the peripheral device and, in response, releasing at least one communication association, resource allocation, or connection state associated with the dockee, the peripheral device, or a docking session. The method may further include receiving a joining request from the dockee or the peripheral device and processing the joining request to permit participation in an existing wireless group or docking session.

In one implementation, the docking center is configured to operate simultaneously in multiple wireless roles. For example, the docking center may operate as a group owner with respect to a first wireless group including the dockee or the peripheral device, while concurrently operating as a client in a second wireless group associated with another device. By operating simultaneously as both a group owner and a client, the docking center enables communication bridging, coordination, or connection assistance between devices that may otherwise be members of different groups or may not be directly connected to one another.

The method thereby enables efficient docking-based connectivity between a dockee and one or more peripheral devices, supports dynamic joining and release of devices, and permits the docking center to coordinate communications across multiple wireless roles or groups.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
